# 7496 - 5-bit shift register

Package DIP-16 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/7496.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/7496.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 22 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![7496 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/7496.png) | ![7496 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/block-7496.png) | ![7496 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/block-7496.png) |

A rectangle for the whole function (or one section of it). Pin numbers are written on the lines where they meet the box; signal names are written beside them.

How to tell it on a drawing: Read the part type from the parts list and compare the pin numbers against this cut-out.

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

## Pins

| Pin | Name | Role | Active | Output type | Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CLOCK | clock |  |  | rising edge |
| 2 | A | input | high |  | acts at once (not clocked); controls pins 15; preset input of stage A: sets it to 1 at once while PE is high |
| 3 | B | input | high |  | acts at once (not clocked); controls pins 14; preset input of stage B: sets it to 1 at once while PE is high |
| 4 | C | input | high |  | acts at once (not clocked); controls pins 13; preset input of stage C: sets it to 1 at once while PE is high |
| 5 | VCC | power |  |  | +5 V |
| 6 | D | input | high |  | acts at once (not clocked); controls pins 11; preset input of stage D: sets it to 1 at once while PE is high |
| 7 | E | input | high |  | acts at once (not clocked); controls pins 10; preset input of stage E: sets it to 1 at once while PE is high |
| 8 | PE | input | high |  | acts at once (not clocked); controls pins 15, 14, 13, 11, 10; PRESET ENABLE: while high, every stage whose preset input is high is set to 1 |
| 9 | SER | input |  |  |  |
| 10 | QE | output |  | totem-pole |  |
| 11 | QD | output |  | totem-pole |  |
| 12 | GND | ground |  |  |  |
| 13 | QC | output |  | totem-pole |  |
| 14 | QB | output |  | totem-pole |  |
| 15 | QA | output |  | totem-pole |  |
| 16 | CLEAR | input | low |  | acts at once (not clocked); controls pins 15, 14, 13, 11, 10; low sets all five stages to 0 at once while the preset is inactive |

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | QA = stateA | Register stage A. |
| 14 | QB = stateB | Register stage B. |
| 13 | QC = stateC | Register stage C. |
| 11 | QD = stateD | Register stage D. |
| 10 | QE = stateE | Register stage E. |

## Stored state

Bits stored: 5

Changes on: rising edge of CLOCK

- Clear and preset do not depend on the clock
- CLEAR low, PE low: QA-QE = 0 at once
- CLEAR low, all preset inputs A-E low (PE don't care): QA-QE = 0
- CLEAR high, PE high: each stage whose preset input is high is set to 1 at once; a stage whose preset input is low holds
- CLEAR high, PE low, CLOCK low: hold
- CLEAR high, PE low, rising edge of CLOCK: QA = SER, QB = old QA, QC = old QB, QD = old QC, QE = old QD
- Parallel load: clear first, then apply data on A-E and a high pulse on PE

## Electrical

| Value | Figure |
|---|---|
| outputLowMaxCurrentMa | 16 |
| outputHighMaxCurrentMa | -0.4 |
| inputSchmitt | no |

## Propagation delays

All measured at VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 15 pF, RL 400 ohm.

| From | To | Edge | Typ ns | Max ns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLOCK | any Q | PLH | 25 | 40 |
| CLOCK | any Q | PHL | 25 | 40 |
| preset or PE | any Q | PLH | 28 | 35 |
| CLEAR | any Q | PHL |  | 55 |

## Timing limits

| What | Pin | Against | Min ns | Min MHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pulse width | CLOCK |  | 35 |  |
| pulse width | CLEAR,PE |  | 30 |  |
| setup | SER | CLOCK rising | 30 |  |
| hold | SER | CLOCK rising | 0 |  |
| max clock frequency | CLOCK |  |  | 10 |

## Not known

- Result when CLEAR is low while PE and a preset input are both high: not in the function table.
- Typical delay from CLEAR: the table gives the maximum (55 ns) only.

## Notes

The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delays; the path-delay function uses 0 ns for the minimum.
